title: Determinants of Psychological Outcomes Following Intensive Care Treatment in Patients with Cardiogenic Shock
summary:
The presence of heart disease can affect not only physical health but also mental and psychological well-being. One reason for this is that experiencing a cardiac event is often accompanied by feelings of helplessness and even fear of death. In addition, the symptoms caused by heart disease can negatively impact daily life. To date, little attention has been paid in cardiological follow-up care to the emotional burden associated with the disease, resulting in many of these symptoms remaining undetected and untreated.
We assume that patients who have survived cardiogenic shock are particularly at increased risk of developing psychological sequelae. Cardiogenic shock is a severe cardiac event that necessitates intensive care treatment.
At present, it is unclear which aspects of intensive care therapy contribute to a persistent deterioration in mental health following hospital discharge.
The aim of this study is to investigate mental health outcomes after survival of a severe cardiac event. Specifically, we seek to identify potentially distressing factors associated with intensive care treatment. By doing so, we hope to contribute to future improvements in the treatment of heart disease and reduce the occurrence of psychological comorbidities.
We will use five different questionnaires to assess psychological symptoms. These questionnaires will be completed at several time points following treatment. In addition, laboratory analyses will be performed to determine the concentrations of biomarkers that may play an important role in the development of mental health disorders.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients may participate in this study if they:
• required intensive care treatment due to cardiogenic shock.
• were treated in the intensive care unit for at least 48 hours.
• are of legal age.
• are mentally and physically capable of understanding the significance and implications of the study and following the instructions of the study staff.
• have the legal capacity to consent and have signed the informed consent form.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients cannot participate in the study if they:
• are minors
• suffer from a pre-existing cognitive impairment resulting in a lack of legal capacity
• have a pre-existing neurological condition causing severe impairment in daily life
• are receiving pharmacological treatment for a pre-existing mental illness
• are suspected of having hypoxic brain damage
• have a history of alcohol or drug abuse
• are expected to be unwilling to actively participate in study-related procedures
• are institutionalized by order of an authority or court
• have a relationship of dependency or employment with the investigator or their deputy
• are non-German speakers with insufficient English proficiency for whose native language no qualified translator is available, such that it must be assumed the content of the questionnaires cannot be adequately understood
